text.arabic_uthmani: وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦ يَٰقَوْمِ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ جَعَلَ فِيكُمْ أَنۢبِيَآءَ وَجَعَلَكُم مُّلُوكًۭا وَءَاتَىٰكُم مَّا لَمْ يُؤْتِ أَحَدًۭا مِّنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle that carries the discourse into a recalled scene
words.prose: he term does more than continue the line. It carries the prior discourse into a remembered Mosaic scene, so the capability and warning around 5:19 are answered by a concrete history of divine benefaction.

topics.headline: discourse carried into remembered proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 5:20 is not a detached new address but a remembered proof brought forward from the boundary after 5:19.
topics.reason: The local clause evidence treats {{ar:وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ}} ({{tr:wa-idh qāla mūsā li-qawmihī}}) as a remembered time of speech, supporting the transition claim.

words.gloss_range: outer temporal recollection particle
words.prose: The first 	he term opens the outer memory frame. Because another 	he term appears at word 13, the verse stages memory twice: first the narrated occasion of Moses speaking, then the contents he commands his people to remember.

topics.headline: outer memory before inner memory
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices two temporal layers, the Qur'anic report of Moses' speech and Moses' own command to internalize the favors.
topics.reason: The first temporal clause covers words 1-6, while the later temporal subordinator introduces the explanatory favor clause at words 13-16.

words.gloss_range: reported saying that introduces an imperative quotation
words.root_gloss_range: speech, utterance, declaration, and voiced position; the local frame selects reported speech with exhortative force
words.prose: he term presents Moses' address as a completed remembered speech, but the quoted content makes it more than neutral reporting. The verb takes 	he term before the quotation, so the target community is fixed before the imperative appears; the Mosaic address formula also recalls a correction-and-reminder register such as 2:54, while 5:12 gives the surah another covenantal speech frame.

topics.headline: reported speech with command force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the remembered saying reactivates an old command rather than merely quoting historical information.
topics.reason: Attachment marks the direct utterance as the complement of {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}), and the quoted unit begins with vocative plus imperative.

topics.headline: community fixed before quotation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that all later second-person plural forms first belong to Moses' people inside the narrated scene.
topics.reason: The lām-governed addressee phrase is syntactically attached to the speech verb before the quotation opens.

topics.headline: Mosaic communal address register
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a recognizable Mosaic communal-address pattern that links this reminder with correction scenes such as 2:54 and with covenantal speech in 5:12.
topics.reason: The formulaic claim survives as an intertextual register cue; it does not override the local syntax of the quotation.

words.gloss_range: foreign proper name of the prophetic speaker
words.prose: he term anchors the scene in a named prophetic speaker rather than an abstract teacher. His name remains a foreign proper noun in Arabic, so biographical associations may color the name without turning it into a local Arabic root argument; at the same time, he himself embodies the prophetic presence he later names among the people. The surrounding 	he term and 	he term make the benefits Israelite memory inside Moses' own address, with related Mosaic address registers visible at 2:54 and 7:128.

topics.headline: foreign name, not Arabic root proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the biographical concreteness of Moses' name while avoiding an overread Arabic derivation.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as a foreign proper noun; supplied etymological associations may be retained only as background color.

topics.headline: speaker exemplifies the favor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Moses is not just reporting prophethood; his speech is itself a living instance of the prophetic favor.
topics.reason: Moses is the subject of the speech verb, and the first listed favor is prophets placed among the same addressed people.

topics.headline: Mosaic memory enters present admonition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the admonition reaches later hearers through Israel's own Mosaic memory, with address patterns comparable to 2:54 and 7:128.
topics.reason: The named speaker is surrounded by third-person and vocative community language, and the discourse shifts from direct divine address into narrated prophetic speech.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the addressee of speech
words.prose: he term marks Moses speaking to his people. Its job here is not possession by itself, but addressee targeting: the community is grammatically placed before the quoted words arrive.

topics.headline: speech target, not mere possession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the people are targeted as hearers before they are summoned in direct address.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks {{ar:لِقَوْمِهِ}} ({{tr:li-qawmihī}}) as the addressee complement of {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}).

words.gloss_range: his people as the governed addressee community
words.root_gloss_range: standing, rising, being established, and a constituted people; local use is communal identity under address
words.prose: The first 	he term, understood in the phrase 	he term, introduces the people as Moses' governed addressees. The suffix fixes the referent before the later vocative, and the root's standing-field gives the community a responsible collective stance without reducing the noun to etymology alone.

topics.headline: his people before my people
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the later direct address does not introduce a new audience; it intensifies the same people already framed as Moses' own.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive under the preposition and bears the third-person possessive relation before the quote shifts to second-person address.

topics.headline: constituted people under address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the addressees as a constituted people expected to stand responsibly under remembered favor.
topics.reason: The root image can color communal responsibility, but local grammar selects the ordinary noun for Moses' people.

topics.headline: narration turns into address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from the narrator's third-person frame to Moses' second-person intimacy without changing the group.
topics.reason: The same communal noun occurs before and inside direct speech, producing a controlled shift in voice.

words.gloss_range: vocative particle initiating direct address
words.prose: he term pulls the recalled speech into direct address. Before the command to remember is issued, attention is secured and the historical report becomes a face-to-face summons.

topics.headline: direct address opens the command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the scene becoming immediate at the exact point Moses names his people.
topics.reason: Attachment marks the vocative as the addressee of the imperative that follows.

words.gloss_range: vocative my people, with elided possessive in the base reading
words.root_gloss_range: standing, rising, being established, and a people; local use is direct communal address
words.prose: In 	he term, the community becomes Moses' direct addressee as my people. The base form carries the possessive relation compactly, while the accepted case variant changes parsing without changing the addressee. The prophetic formula aligns Moses with other direct communal calls, including 7:59, 7:65, 7:73, and 7:85.

topics.headline: my people in compact vocative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the summons is intimate and communal, not merely administrative.
topics.reason: The noun is locally the vocative addressee of the imperative and carries first-person possessive force in the base reading.

topics.headline: variant case, same addressee
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accepted case variation affects syntax but not the identity of the summoned people.
topics.reason: The variant is useful for parsing contrast, while the local attachment still identifies the same vocative addressee.

topics.headline: shared prophetic call
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices Moses speaking in a broader prophetic address formula also used by Noah, Hud, Salih, and Shuayb in 7:59, 7:65, 7:73, and 7:85.
topics.reason: The formulaic comparison survives as a register cue; locally it remains Moses' direct vocative.

words.gloss_range: plural imperative to remember and mention
words.root_gloss_range: remembering, mentioning, reminding, and keeping present; local use commands collective recollection and articulation
words.prose: he term is a second-person plural imperative, so remembrance is imposed on the community as an action. The root allows both inward recall and verbal mention; accepted intensifying recitation evidence sharpens the pressure toward taking heed without replacing the base imperative. In the surah, the formula recurs at 5:7, 5:11, and 5:20, and it answers the failure of forgetting described at 5:13-14.

topics.headline: collective commanded memory
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the favor list is demanded remembrance, not detached historiography.
topics.reason: The imperative has plural agreement and governs {{ar:نِعْمَةَ}} ({{tr:niʿmata}}) as its direct object.

topics.headline: recall becomes articulation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command asks the people to keep the favor present both inwardly and outwardly.
topics.reason: The lexical range supports remembrance and mention, while local grammar selects the command to remember the favor.

topics.headline: intensified taking-heed as variant pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accepted variant evidence can make the command feel more inwardly forceful, while the base reading remains direct remembering.
topics.reason: The variant is valid contrastive evidence for intensity, but it does not govern the base local parse.

topics.headline: surah refrain against forgetting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 5:20 participates in a repeated favor-remembrance formula at 5:7, 5:11, and 5:20, set against covenantal forgetting at 5:13-14.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows provide concrete same-surah references, and the local formula exactly commands remembrance of Allah's favor.

words.gloss_range: the favor or benefaction to be remembered
words.root_gloss_range: favor, bounty, comfort, ease, affirmation, livestock, and other branch senses; local noun selects divine favor while retaining comfort and bounty color
words.prose: he term is the direct object of the command: the favor itself must be remembered. Its singular form gathers three coordinated benefits into one covenantal benefaction, while the root field of ease, bounty, and tangible provision gives the word embodied warmth without activating unrelated branches such as livestock as the local sense. The formula belongs to the surah's favor architecture at 5:3, 5:7, 5:11, 5:20, and 5:110.

topics.headline: favor as command object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the following history is governed by a command to remember divine favor.
topics.reason: Attachment identifies {{ar:نِعْمَةَ}} ({{tr:niʿmata}}) as the explicit object of {{ar:ٱذْكُرُوا۟}} ({{tr:udhkurū}}).

topics.headline: ease and bounty color the favor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the favor is not a thin abstraction; it carries a field of gracious ease, bounty, and tangible benefaction.
topics.reason: V4 shows multiple branches, so comfort and bounty can color the noun while livestock and other remote branches remain inactive locally.

topics.headline: one favor unfolding in three benefits
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices one singular favor unfolding as prophets among them, kingship made for them, and a unique gift given to them.
topics.reason: The singular noun precedes coordinated explanatory favor clauses at words 13-27.

topics.headline: favor motif across the surah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices 5:20 within a same-surah favor pattern that includes completion at 5:3, remembrance at 5:7 and 5:11, and favor upon Jesus at 5:110.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows give concrete same-surah references and the local phrase matches the favor-remembrance formula.

words.gloss_range: Allah as genitive source of the favor
words.root_gloss_range: deity, worship, devotion, and turning; local proper name identifies Allah as the source of favor
words.prose: he term binds the favor to Allah through construct grammar. That attachment fixes the source before the later verbs of making and giving, so prophets, status, and the unmatched gift are not communal achievements detached from divine agency. The same named giver links this Mosaic speech to the surah's favor-remembrance pattern at 5:7, 5:11, and 5:20 and to divine giving in 5:48.

topics.headline: favor grammatically belongs to Allah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the source of every listed benefit is fixed before the benefits are named.
topics.reason: Attachment marks {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) as genitive dependent of {{ar:نِعْمَةَ}} ({{tr:niʿmata}}).

topics.headline: proper name with worshipful gravity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine name gives the benefits theological gravity while remaining a proper name in local grammar.
topics.reason: Derivational discussion can supply semantic gravity, but QAC and local syntax treat the word as the divine proper name.

topics.headline: divine agency governs all gifts
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that even the unmatched scope of the gift and the making verbs remain anchored to divine benefaction, with giving language also visible at 5:48 and making language contrasted at 5:13.
topics.reason: The later verbs lack a fresh overt subject noun, so the construct phrase keeps divine source explicit for the whole favor complex.

topics.headline: named giver across memory formulas
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Moses' phrase names the same giver inside the favor-remembrance refrain at 5:7, 5:11, and 5:20.
topics.reason: The rows provide concrete same-surah formula references; the local phrase matches the repeated memory command.

words.gloss_range: upon you, marking favor as resting on the addressed group
words.prose: he term makes the favor rest upon the addressees. The preposition's overness lets grace and obligation meet: what is placed upon them is also a burden of memory. Its suffix begins the chain continued by 	he term, 	he term, and 	he term, while the larger discourse invites later hearers to align with ancestral memory without collapsing the audiences.

topics.headline: favor resting as obligation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that favor is pictured as something laid upon the community, joining grace to accountability.
topics.reason: Attachment says {{ar:عَلَيْكُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalaykum}}) qualifies the favor as upon the addressees.

topics.headline: second-person chain through the favors
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same addressed body carried through the clauses: upon you, among you, made you, and gave you.
topics.reason: The recurring second-person plural suffix is locally visible in successive prepositional and verbal attachments.

topics.headline: ancestral memory without audience collapse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that present address can be aligned with Mosaic memory while the immediate historical referent remains Moses' people.
topics.reason: The quoted speech frame fixes the immediate referent, while the discourse boundary supports alignment rather than direct referent substitution.

words.gloss_range: inner temporal subordinator explaining the favor
words.prose: The second 	he term pivots from the command to remember the favor into the historical acts that define it. It does not start an independent narrative; it subordinates the first favor clause and opens the nested memory of prophets placed among the people.

topics.headline: favor content begins
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the following acts explain the one favor rather than adding a separate scene.
topics.reason: Attachment marks words 13-16 as a temporal explanatory clause under the quoted command.

words.gloss_range: made, placed, or appointed; here placed prophets among the people
words.root_gloss_range: creating, making, placing, appointing, rendering, and arranging; local complement selects internal placement for the first occurrence
words.prose: The first 	he term begins the explained favor with completed divine action. Its complement 	he term selects the placement side of the verb's range: prophets are placed among the people, not merely sent toward them. This differs from the second 	he term, where the same root shifts into direct transformation, and it turns the divine capability emphasized around 5:19 into remembered social formation.

topics.headline: same verb, different construction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the two making verbs should not be flattened: one places prophets among them, the other makes them kings or possessors.
topics.reason: Local attachment gives the first verb a locative complement and the second a direct object plus result predicate.

topics.headline: completed act of favor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the remembered favor rests on accomplished divine action rather than future promise.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment identify the verb as perfect Form I in the remembered favor clause.

topics.headline: prophets placed among them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices prophethood as internal divine emplacement within the community, not a distant message dispatched from outside.
topics.reason: The locative phrase {{ar:فِيكُمْ}} ({{tr:fīkum}}) licenses the placing branch of the broad making verb.

topics.headline: positive making inside broader divine action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this positive making against other same-surah making language where divine arrangement can expose judgment or testing.
topics.reason: The same-root recurrence is a contextual echo; local syntax still controls this occurrence as positive placement.

words.gloss_range: among you or within you, locating prophets inside the addressed community
words.prose: he term supplies the locative frame for the first making verb. The suffix points back to the people summoned as 	he term, and the preposition moves the favor from being upon them to being among them: prophetic presence becomes an internal communal endowment.

topics.headline: prophets among the addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that prophethood is located inside the very group being commanded to remember.
topics.reason: Attachment identifies {{ar:فِيكُمْ}} ({{tr:fīkum}}) as the prepositional complement of the first {{ar:جَعَلَ}} ({{tr:jaʿala}}).

topics.headline: external favor becomes internal endowment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a grammatical shift from favor upon the people to prophets among the people.
topics.reason: The second-person suffix continues from {{ar:عَلَيْكُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿalaykum}}) into a different prepositional relation.

words.gloss_range: prophets as an indefinite plural class placed among the people
words.root_gloss_range: news-bearing, prophecy, and debated elevation associations; local plural names prophets as bearers of revelatory communication with possible elevated-status coloring
words.prose: he term names the first explained favor: prophets placed among the people. Its indefinite broken plural stresses a class and multiplicity rather than a closed named list. The lexical dispute between news-bearing and elevation can survive as pressure, but locally the strongest payoff is revelatory communication embedded within the community, especially after messenger language at 5:19 and before the parallel status noun 	he term.

topics.headline: plural class of prophets
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices multiplicity and institutional presence rather than a list of named prophets.
topics.reason: QAC and noun-instance evidence mark the word as an indefinite broken plural.

topics.headline: prophets are what God placed among them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the prophets as the specified object of internal placement, not as distant messengers sent from outside.
topics.reason: Attachment makes {{ar:أَنۢبِيَآءَ}} ({{tr:anbiyāʾa}}) the object of {{ar:جَعَلَ}} ({{tr:jaʿala}}), with {{ar:فِيكُمْ}} ({{tr:fīkum}}) as locative complement.

topics.headline: news-bearing with elevated-status coloring
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices prophetic presence as revelatory communication, with the classical elevation discussion adding status pressure without displacing the news-bearing sense.
topics.reason: The root dispute is real, but local context favors communication because the word sits inside a speech and remembrance frame.

topics.headline: messenger language becomes embedded prophethood
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices continuity from messenger language and warning-good-news functions at 5:19 into prophets placed among Moses' people at 5:20.
topics.reason: The boundary rows provide concrete reference to 5:19, while local syntax keeps this word inside Moses' recalled favor list.

topics.headline: prophets and kings as paired favors
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices prophetic presence and royal or possessive status as parallel indefinite plural outcomes of divine making.
topics.reason: The two nouns stand after adjacent making clauses and share indefinite accusative plural behavior.

topics.headline: prophethood echoes speech and memory
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Moses' own speech, the command to remember, and prophets among the people reinforce one communicative field.
topics.reason: The local frame is built from speech, vocative, imperative remembrance, and a named prophetic speaker.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle linking the second favor clause
words.prose: This 	he term attaches the second favor without subordinating it to the first. The making of the people as 	he term runs parallel to prophets placed among them, so both belong to the one favor complex.

topics.headline: second favor in parallel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices kingship or possessive status as a coordinated favor, not a subordinate afterthought to prophethood.
topics.reason: Attachment treats {{ar:وَجَعَلَكُم مُلُوكًا}} ({{tr:wa-jaʿalakum mulūkan}}) as a coordinated second favor clause.

words.gloss_range: made you, with direct object suffix and result complement
words.root_gloss_range: making, placing, appointing, rendering, and transforming; local construction selects rendering the people into a status
words.prose: he term shifts the repeated making verb from placement among the people to transformation of the people themselves. The suffix targets the same addressees already fixed by 	he term and 	he term, and 	he term states the resulting role. The progression is among you, then you yourselves.

topics.headline: same people become the object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second favor lands directly on the same community's identity.
topics.reason: Attachment marks the suffix as object, and the prior discourse fixes its referent as Moses' addressed people.

topics.headline: made you into kings or possessors
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices social status as an effect of divine making, not innate communal possession.
topics.reason: Attachment and translation support identify a direct object plus result predicate structure.

topics.headline: from among you to you yourselves
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices escalation from internal provision to direct communal transformation.
topics.reason: The adjacent clauses repeat the same root while changing valency from locative placement to object-result transformation.

words.gloss_range: kings, possessors, or holders of granted authority in the result-predicate frame
words.root_gloss_range: royal authority, possession, mastery, dominion, firmness, and related branches; local plural allows kingship or possessive authority while divine making keeps it derivative
words.prose: he term is the result complement: it names what the addressees are made. Its indefinite broken plural distributes status across the community rather than naming one monarch. The root can hold royal authority, possession, mastery, and dominion, so the title may hover between literal kings and possessors of autonomy, but the making verb keeps all human authority derivative from Allah. This stands under the surah's sovereignty frame, including divine dominion in 5:17-18, and can be compared with Solomon's unique dominion request at 38:35 without collapsing the two.

topics.headline: what they are made
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word names the resulting status of the people, not a separate possession beside them.
topics.reason: Attachment marks the noun as the second object or result predicate of {{ar:جَعَلَكُم}} ({{tr:jaʿalakum}}).

topics.headline: distributed status, not one dynasty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices communal distribution of status rather than a single dynastic title.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an indefinite broken plural in accusative result position.

topics.headline: kingship and possessive authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word can carry both royal and possession-like authority, while local grammar keeps it a granted status.
topics.reason: The classical range supports kingship and possession; local result-predicate syntax and the making verb prevent treating authority as innate or absolute.

topics.headline: human authority under divine dominion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices human authority in 5:20 as delegated under Allah's dominion asserted in 5:17-18.
topics.reason: The same-surah sovereignty frame qualifies local human status without negating the granted title.

topics.headline: communal grant compared with unique dominion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a useful contrast between communal granted status here and Solomon's singular request for unmatched dominion at 38:35.
topics.reason: The comparison is valid as contrast, but local {{ar:مُلُوكًۭا}} ({{tr:mulūkan}}) remains a communal plural status in 5:20.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle introducing the third favor
words.prose: This 	he term coordinates the third favor with the two making clauses. It keeps the item in the same enumeration while allowing a new verbal mode: from making and transforming to giving an unnamed, incomparable grant.

topics.headline: third favor in the same chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final gift as part of the same favor chain while also hearing its shift into comparative uniqueness.
topics.reason: Attachment treats {{ar:وَءَاتَىٰكُم}} ({{tr:wa-ātākum}}) as a coordinated third favor clause with its own relative comparison.

words.gloss_range: gave you or caused to reach you, with the community as recipient and the relative object as gift
words.root_gloss_range: coming, bringing, arriving, giving, and causing to come; Form IV locally selects giving as caused arrival to recipients
words.prose: he term shifts the enumeration from making to giving. In Form IV, the root's coming-field lets the gift be pictured as something caused to reach the community; the suffix marks the same addressed body as recipient, and 	he term supplies the received object. The word then meets 	he term in a same-root contrast: gave you, but did not give anyone else. With the unnamed object and universal exclusion, the third favor becomes the ayah's climax of comparative uniqueness.

topics.headline: you receive the unnamed grant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same collective body becoming the recipient of a still-unnamed gift.
topics.reason: Attachment marks the suffix and {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) as the two object roles of the giving verb.

topics.headline: gave you, did not give anyone else
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices uniqueness made audible through the same root in affirmation and negation.
topics.reason: The local clause sets perfect affirmative {{ar:ءَاتَىٰكُم}} ({{tr:ātākum}}) against lam-negated {{ar:يُؤْتِ}} ({{tr:yuʾti}}).

topics.headline: gift as caused arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices giving as a delivered arrival to the community, not a static possession.
topics.reason: Form IV supports causative giving from the broader coming root, and local syntax selects transitive bestowal.

topics.headline: divine giving differentiates communities
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this gift-language within a surah theology of divine bestowal and differentiated accountability, including scripture and law in 5:48.
topics.reason: The same-surah comparison is concrete and compatible with the local giving frame.

topics.headline: from constitution to unique bestowal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the list climbing from making and status to an unnamed gift powerful because it is both bestowed on them and withheld from all others.
topics.reason: The coordinated sequence moves from two making clauses to a giving clause completed by relative negated comparison.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun heading the unnamed received object
words.prose: he term is the object head of the gift, but it leaves the content unnamed. The following negated clause defines the gift by comparison rather than inventory, so the focus falls on uniqueness: what matters is that no one else among the worlds received it in that way.

topics.headline: unnamed gift defined by exclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the gift magnified by being left unnamed and then measured through universal negation.
topics.reason: Attachment marks {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) as the object of {{ar:ءَاتَىٰكُم}} ({{tr:ātākum}}) and the head of the relative clause.

words.gloss_range: jussive negator giving past negative force to the following verb
words.prose: he term turns the following imperfect verb into past negation. The comparison is therefore not simply that no one is receiving it now, but that no comparable grant had been given to anyone else; the third favor is exceptional, not merely additional.

topics.headline: past negation marks exceptionality
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparison depends on a past-negative claim of unmatched giving.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as governing a jussive imperfect, and attachment places the negated verb inside the relative comparison.

words.gloss_range: he give, jussive after negation; locally not-given in the comparative relative clause
words.root_gloss_range: coming, bringing, giving, and causing to come; Form IV locally repeats the giving root under negation
words.prose: he term is the jussive imperfect after 	he term. It governs 	he term as recipient while 	he term supplies the implicit thing not given. Because it repeats the Form IV giving root from 	he term, the contrast becomes audible: given to you, not given to anyone else.

topics.headline: jussive form creates past negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the morphology is essential to reading the comparison as a past-negative exclusion.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as imperfect jussive after {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}).

topics.headline: no comparable recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the favor's meaning depends on exclusion as much as on bestowal.
topics.reason: The verb governs {{ar:أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}) inside the relative clause defining what was not given.

topics.headline: given and not-given sound alike
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices root-level antithesis binding the third favor to its negated comparison.
topics.reason: Both verbs use the same Form IV giving root across affirmation and negation in one sentence.

words.gloss_range: anyone at all under negation
words.root_gloss_range: one, anyone, oneness, and emphatic exclusion under negation; local use selects anyone-at-all as recipient excluded from comparable giving
words.prose: he term is the object-recipient of the negated giving verb. Under negation, its singular indefinite form becomes anyone at all, so the comparison blocks every rival recipient without needing an explicit exception particle. The formula 	he term also returns in 5:115, where unparalleled gift and unparalleled consequence become thematic counterweights; it can be compared with Solomon's unmatched dominion request at 38:35 without collapsing communal and individual uniqueness.

topics.headline: no one as direct recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices exclusion made syntactically direct: no one was given the comparable gift.
topics.reason: Attachment identifies {{ar:أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}) as the object of {{ar:يُؤْتِ}} ({{tr:yuʾti}}).

topics.headline: absolute exclusion under negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase means not anyone at all, not merely zero counted recipients.
topics.reason: Contextual profiles show this form often under negation, and local {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) supplies that negative scope.

topics.headline: gift and consequence formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same unparalleled formula in 5:20 for gift and in 5:115 for consequence.
topics.reason: The rows provide an identical concrete same-surah phrase, and local syntax supports the formulaic comparison.

topics.headline: communal uniqueness not Solomon's request
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a contrast with Solomon's individual unmatched dominion request at 38:35 while keeping 5:20's claim communal.
topics.reason: The comparison is useful for uniqueness language, but local grammar concerns the gift to Moses' addressed people.

words.gloss_range: from or among, introducing the comparison domain
words.prose: he term introduces the domain from which anyone else is excluded. By delaying the phrase to the end, the verse first says no one, then maximizes the scope: no one from among the worlds.

topics.headline: universal domain introduced
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparison is scoped over a named universal class, not vague superiority.
topics.reason: Attachment marks {{ar:مِنَ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ}} ({{tr:mina l-ʿālamīn}}) as restricting {{ar:أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}).

words.gloss_range: the worlds as the definite comparison domain
words.root_gloss_range: worlds, peoples, created orders, and sign-bearing or knowledge-linked domains; local phrase selects the broad comparison domain under negation
words.prose: he term closes the ayah with the widest comparison domain. It is genitive after 	he term, definite, and plural, so the exclusion is measured against the known total field of worlds, peoples, or created orders. The root's sign-bearing and knowledge associations can color the cosmic register, especially with the familiar 	he term formula at 1:2, while the same unparalleled wording in 5:115 makes 5:20's gift and 5:115's consequence answer one another inside the surah.

topics.headline: the governed world-domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the worlds as the definite domain over which the negated giving is evaluated.
topics.reason: Attachment marks the noun as genitive governed by {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}), restricting {{ar:أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}).

topics.headline: cosmic and sign-bearing register
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the comparison expanding beyond neighboring peoples into ordered, sign-bearing created domains.
topics.reason: The broader root field can color the noun, but local syntax selects it as the comparison domain.

topics.headline: maximum restrictive scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final cadence widening the exclusion to all worlds, not only a nation or generation.
topics.reason: The plural definite noun closes the negated comparison and maximizes the domain of exclusion.

topics.headline: worlds formula echoes and returns
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices 5:20's historical favor measured against the cosmic register of 1:2 and echoed by the unparalleled consequence formula in 5:115.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete formulaic references to 1:2 and 5:115, while local grammar remains the final comparison phrase.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The imperative to remember the blessing is unpacked by the repeated temporal frame and the sequence 'made ... made ... gave.'
baseline_models.mechanism: Remembering is not a vague feeling but the reconstruction of a layered bestowal: prophetic mediation was installed within the people, the addressees were assigned royal standing, and an exhaustively unmatched gift was transferred to them.

activation_trace.role: Heart-level retrieval after possible forgetting makes the following clauses the content to be actively reassembled.
Good condition and benefaction name the sequence as a favorable state bestowed upon the addressees.
Twice making something assume a condition organizes prophets and kings as constituted statuses rather than accidental possessions.
The one who reports from God supplies the internal mediation component of the bestowed order.
Kingship and governing authority supply the public agency component of the bestowed order.
The positive and negated forms of giving frame the final gift as an actual transfer and a denied comparison.
Indefinite 'anyone' under negation exhausts the comparison class and intensifies the gift's singularity.

changed_reading.before: Moses generally asks the people to remember that God favored them.
changed_reading.after: Moses asks them to reconstruct a specific constitutional sequence of internal guidance, conferred agency, and incomparable provision.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The asymmetry between 'made among you prophets' and 'made you kings.'
baseline_models.mechanism: Prophetic report is placed inside the collective, while royal possession or disposal is predicated directly of the plural addressees. The pair can therefore form a distributed architecture: guidance is internally available and agency is broadly assigned.

activation_trace.role: Constitutive making links two differently distributed social capacities.
Reporting from God provides the collective's internally located channel of direction.
Possession and effective disposal allow 'kings' to activate agency without requiring every addressee to occupy a throne.
The twice-addressed human collective is the shared body across which guidance and agency are distributed.

changed_reading.before: Prophets and kings are two honorific achievements in national history.
changed_reading.after: The people were equipped with a two-part social capacity: divine reporting from within and effective agency across the addressed collective.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The plural 'made you kings' addressed to the whole people.
baseline_models.mechanism: Root branches of strength, cohesion, and the supporting core of an affair permit a functional reading of kingship as collective self-maintenance. Royal language may mark people made able to hold their affairs together, not only people supplied with palace rulers.

activation_trace.role: Strength and cohesion make kingship an image of a people able to remain structurally intact.
The supporting core of an affair gives royal status the functional role of carrying communal order.
A sustaining basis or livelihood links the addressed people to the practical conditions by which a collective stands.

changed_reading.before: God supplied the people with monarchs.
changed_reading.after: God may also be naming a people made capable of holding, supporting, and administering their own collective affair.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The positive 'gave you' is answered by 'did not give anyone among the worlds.'
baseline_models.mechanism: The repeated giving verb and exhaustive negative comparison make the special object potentially the whole preceding configuration rather than an unnamed quantity. Its force is patterned incomparability: no comparator received this same conjunction of gifts.

activation_trace.role: Repeated giving binds the positive grant and its unmatched negative counterpart into one comparison.
Exhaustive scope under negation makes the comparison categorical rather than merely superlative.

changed_reading.before: They received an exceptionally large but unspecified favor.
changed_reading.after: They received an unmatched configuration whose singularity may consist in the conjunction of internal prophecy, royal agency, and further provision.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening demand to fulfill binding contracts and the later near-verbatim repetition of 'remember God's blessing upon you' beside the confirmed covenant convert recollection into covenant renewal. Remembered gifts supply the grounds and capacity for pledged obedience.

activation_trace.role: The focus imperative performs active retrieval of the bestowed order.
Full completion without deficiency establishes performance, not sentiment, as the pericope's opening demand.
A binding, ratified obligation supplies the legal-social form toward which remembered blessing can move.
The emphatic covenant directly joins the repeated blessing formula to an enacted pledge.
The same retrieval action repeats before the covenant response, resolving the focus imperative as a renewal practice.
The repeated benefaction term identifies the good state as covenantally consequential.

structural_cues: 5:1 opens the packet with fulfillment of contracts.
5:7 repeats the focus's imperative-blessing-upon-you formula and immediately adds the covenant and the response 'we hear and obey.'
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies binding, fulfillment, exact formula repetition, and pledged obedience; I infer that recollection renews performance by making gift into obligation. A live alternative is that blessing and covenant are adjacent but independent objects of remembrance.

changed_reading.before: The focus asks for grateful recollection of past privilege.
changed_reading.after: The focus renews a binding relation: remembering how they were equipped is what makes pledged obedience presently actionable.

context_deltas.mechanism: Elsewhere in the packet, blessing reaches completion through a process that removes defilement and culminates in gratitude. The focus list therefore shifts from luxury or rank to formation: prophets, kingship, and giving are capacities meant to bring a people into a usable, responsive condition.

activation_trace.role: The focus's favorable condition becomes the process whose completion the context specifies.
Reaching full completion makes blessing developmental rather than a static possession.
The same benefaction root explicitly names what is brought to completion.
Purity as removal of contamination supplies the transformative operation within completed blessing.
Completion links the bodily practice directly to the maturation of blessing.
Repeated blessing carries the focus noun into an embodied formation sequence.
Recognition and praise of the benefactor provide the intended human output of completed blessing.

structural_cues: 5:3 says the blessing was completed upon the addressees.
5:6 coordinates purification, completion of blessing, and the purpose 'so that you may give thanks.'
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated completion-of-blessing formulas and a purification-to-gratitude sequence; I transfer that process shape to the focus's gift list. A live alternative is that each blessing is a separate favor and the process in 5:6 should not govern the historical list in 5:20.

changed_reading.before: Prophets, kings, and unmatched gifts are marks of elevated comfort or prestige.
changed_reading.after: They are formative endowments whose point is to make a people cleanly capable of recognition and responsive action.

context_deltas.mechanism: The packet sequences covenant-breaking, hardening, displacement of words, and forgetting part of what had been recalled. Against that chain, the focus imperative becomes a maintenance operation: active remembrance keeps a bestowed social order from unraveling and being redescribed beyond recognition.

activation_trace.role: Active retrieval in the focus supplies the direct counter-operation to contextual forgetting.
Undoing what was tightly built supplies the first failure state that remembrance resists.
The emphatic covenant identifies the structure being undone.
Loss of the heart's softness supplies the affective rigidity produced within the failure sequence.
Deflection from a proper direction makes verbal displacement the interpretive deformation of the broken bond.
The disappearance of remembrance names the cognitive failure opposite the focus command.
What serves as a reminder identifies the material from which a forgotten share was lost.
Forgetting as neglect confirms that the failure can be enacted abandonment, not only failed recall.

structural_cues: 5:13 orders breach, hardening, displacement, and forgetting within one causal sentence.
5:14 repeats forgetting a share of what had been recalled and follows it with durable social hostility.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the ordered failure chain and the exact remember-forget opposition; I infer that 5:20's imperative is prophylactic maintenance for its listed gifts. A live alternative is that it merely recalls a contrastive history after deformation has already occurred.

changed_reading.before: Remembering preserves a flattering account of the past.
changed_reading.after: Remembering preserves the covenantal and semantic integrity of the people's endowments against neglect, hardening, and displacement.

context_deltas.mechanism: Clarification of concealed material, illumination, path-guidance, and a messenger arriving after an interval turn 'prophets among you' into an interruption-resistant repair function. Prophetic presence is valuable because it reopens intelligibility and route when transmission has dimmed or paused.

activation_trace.role: The one reporting from God anchors the contextual disclosure-and-guidance mechanism back in the focus.
Making meaning clear by speech or sign supplies the prophetic repair operation.
Illumination converts disclosure into restored visibility.
Gentle direction to a path turns restored visibility into traversable guidance.
Weakness or stillness after intensity supplies the temporal gap that renewed reporting repairs.

structural_cues: 5:15 presents a messenger who clarifies much of what had been concealed and pairs him with light and a clear book.
5:16 moves from light to paths, while 5:19 explicitly locates the messenger after an interval from messengers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies concealment, clarification, light, path, and temporal interruption; I infer that the plurality 'among you prophets' names a durable repair capacity. A live alternative is that 5:20 only counts past prophetic honor and does not describe a social function.

changed_reading.before: Having prophets is chiefly ancestral prestige.
changed_reading.after: Prophets within a people are recurrent repair points that restore disclosure and a navigable route after concealment or interruption.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the focus, the same ownership root denies effective possession against God and twice assigns dominion over heavens and earth to God, alongside divine creating. Human royal status in 5:20 is therefore conferred and bounded: it is a delegated domain within an encompassing ownership, not autonomous sovereignty.

activation_trace.role: Human kingship is the focus status whose scale the contextual dominion claims delimit.
The contrast between owning nothing against God and God's cosmic dominion establishes an asymmetrical ownership hierarchy.
Creative origination supplies the source from which any subsequent human status must derive.
The repeated cosmic dominion claim stabilizes the frame immediately before human kings are named.

structural_cues: 5:17 asks who can own anything against God, then assigns all cosmic dominion to God.
5:18 repeats God's cosmic dominion immediately before 5:20 calls the people kings.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exact root recurrence, denied counter-ownership, cosmic dominion, and creation; I infer a nested delegation from God to human agents. A live alternative is that cosmic sovereignty and historical human monarchy are simply different registers placed side by side.

changed_reading.before: Being made kings grants self-standing sovereignty.
changed_reading.after: Being made kings grants a real but derivative sphere of disposal whose source, limit, and accountability remain within God's dominion.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate next address moves from remembered endowment to entry, forbids backward reversal, and names loss as the result; the gate counsel then names overcoming as the result of entry. The gifts of 5:20 function as warrants and capacities for forward action at a threshold.

activation_trace.role: Effective possession and disposal supply the agency presumed by the command that follows.
Crossing into an interior turns remembered capacity into a concrete forward act.
Returning toward the prior position supplies the prohibited reversal of the bestowed trajectory.
Turning the back gives bodily form to refusal of the forward commission.
General diminution names the outcome when endowed capacity is reversed instead of exercised.
Overcoming power is presented as emerging on the far side of entry, not as a precondition possessed beforehand.

structural_cues: 5:21 immediately repeats 'O my people' and follows 5:20's list with an entry command.
The sequence opposes enter/overcome to turn-back/lose.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency, repeated address, opposed motion, and opposed outcomes; I infer that the 5:20 inventory is the warrant for 5:21's commission. A live alternative is that the recollection only encourages trust while the command rests independently on the land being written for them.

changed_reading.before: The gifts certify a settled identity already possessed.
changed_reading.after: The gifts certify a capacity that becomes real in forward entry; unused endowment can invert into loss.

context_deltas.mechanism: Perceived coercive power makes the people refuse the gate and choose non-action; Moses then narrows ownership to himself and his brother. The later recurrence of the kingship root operationalizes the earlier plural title: royal capacity begins with command of one's own commitment and coordination with a willing ally, not guaranteed command over others.

activation_trace.role: The focus's conferred possession is the broad claim that the dialogue tests and narrows.
Compulsion and overpowering force supply the rival image of mastery before which the people surrender their own agency.
The entrance reduces an overwhelming field to a bounded point at which agency can be exercised.
Overcoming is predicted as the consequence of taking the bounded action.
Abstention from action is the people's explicit abdication of the agency implied by kingship.
Moses's statement of limited possession supplies a direct lexical narrowing from collective royal status to actionable control.
The self as the thing itself identifies the irreducible first domain over which willing action remains possible.
Brotherhood adds the smallest surviving relation of coordinated agency beyond the individual self.

structural_cues: 5:22-24 moves from fear of overpowering people to refusal of the gate and the declaration 'we are sitting.'
5:25 answers the collective refusal with Moses's 'I possess only myself and my brother.'
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the exact ownership root in 5:20 and 5:25 plus the action/refusal contrast; I infer that the later statement retroactively exposes self-command as a minimum content of kingship. A live alternative is that 'kings' is political-historical while 'I possess only myself' is an unrelated idiom of inability.

changed_reading.before: Kingship means that the people possess political dominance over an external territory.
changed_reading.after: Kingship first means non-transferable command of one's own response and the ability to coordinate willing relations; external dominance is neither automatic nor guaranteed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The exhaustive claim of unmatched giving is followed by threatened loss and finally deprivation of the desired land after refusal. Incomparability therefore increases responsibility but does not create immunity: a gift can authorize access without making its enjoyment unconditional.

activation_trace.role: The unmatched transfer is the endowment whose practical possession the following response tests.
Exhaustive negative comparison heightens distinction without itself guaranteeing continued access.
Diminution is announced as the immediate possible inversion of the privileged position.
Deprivation and failure to obtain the desired object realize the loss that refusal made possible.

structural_cues: 5:21 warns that turning back will make them losers despite the immediately preceding gift list.
5:26 bars the land for forty years and describes wandering; the branchless ت ي ه cue is used structurally, not as a citation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies unmatched giving, a loss warning, refusal, prohibition, and wandering; I infer a gift-to-responsibility arrow rather than gift-to-immunity. A live alternative is that the unmatched gifts are entirely past and unaffected by the later loss of access to land.

changed_reading.before: Unprecedented favor secures an exceptional status regardless of response.
changed_reading.after: Unprecedented favor creates an exceptional obligation to act; distinction can coexist with deprivation when endowed capacity is refused.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the noun 'people' should not simply be replaced by the verbal sense 'rise.' It remains anchored in the repeated ق و م root, its packet branch of resolve and rising, the renewed vocative in 5:21, and the explicit counter-image of sitting in 5:24. Render it only as a root-echo that intensifies the address, not as a lexical translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The doubled 'my people' in 5:20 immediately before the same address and the entry command in 5:21.

activation_trace.role: Resolve and rising toward an affair let the repeated vocative carry latent mobilizing pressure.
The renewed address directly before 'enter' turns the root echo toward a concrete act of rising.
Abstention from action provides the explicit reversal of the vocative's activated rising image.

changed_reading.before: 'O my people' is a neutral kinship address.
changed_reading.after: As a contained root-echo, the repeated address presses 'people capable of rising toward the affair,' making 'we are sitting' a pointed self-negation.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the two men in 5:23 are not identified as prophets, and the reading must not promote them to that office. It remains valid as a functional analogy anchored in 'prophets among you' plus the later appearance of two blessed internal speakers whose counsel requires collective enactment. Render it as a replay of the guidance-agency circuit, never as an identity claim.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The paired focus construction places reporters from God within the people and assigns royal agency to the addressed group.

activation_trace.role: A consequential report arriving to its hearers supplies the guidance side of the focus's social circuit.
Effective disposal supplies the collective action side that must receive and enact internal counsel.
An uttered intervention makes the two insiders' guidance publicly available to the collective.
The two men localize the activating counsel in a small human minority within the larger group.
Benefaction marks the insiders themselves as recipients able to transmit an action-enabling reading.
The entrance converts counsel into a precise collective action point.

changed_reading.before: Prophets and kings are completed historical categories listed in the past.
changed_reading.after: Their functional relation can replay at smaller scale whenever blessed insiders disclose an actionable route and a collectively endowed people must choose whether to enact it.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the branch in which water lets travelers or a camp master their affair, while the ayahs never mention water. It remains anchored directly in the focus's م ل ك inventory and gains a material frame from land, entry, and eventual deprivation. Render it only as a logistical analogy for settlement-capacity, not as the lexical meaning of 'kings' or a historical water claim.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The collective plural 'made you kings' before a command to enter and inhabit a land.

activation_trace.role: Water by which travelers master their affair activates kingship as the material sufficiency needed to control movement and settlement.
Productive, inhabitable ground supplies the settlement domain in which logistical mastery would matter.
Entry supplies the movement by which endowed logistical capacity would become habitation.
Deprivation of the desired land provides the negative material outcome when settlement-capacity is not enacted.

changed_reading.before: Kingship denotes courtly rule over subjects.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, kingship can denote being provisioned with the logistical basis by which a mobile people governs entry, movement, and durable settlement.

strongest_changes: Remembering the blessing became covenant renewal and an anti-deformation practice rather than commemorative gratitude alone.
Kingship became derivative agency bounded by God's dominion and operationally tested as self-command at the gate.
The gift list became capacity for entry whose distinction creates responsibility without guaranteeing immunity from loss.
summary.what_was_special: The context repeatedly turned status nouns into operations: blessing is completed through formation, prophecy repairs interrupted disclosure, kingship is tested by action, and unmatched giving can end in deprivation when its capacity is refused.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether 'made you kings' primarily denotes actual political monarchy, broad possession, self-governance, or a deliberately layered combination remains open.
Whether the final unmatched gift refers to the whole preceding configuration or to an unstated additional object remains grammatically open.
The rising echo in 'my people,' the two-men circuit, and the settlement-logistics model are branch-driven activations and must remain explicitly exploratory.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Kingship names cohesive agency before territory.** `م ل ك B001` supplies strength/cohesion and `B005` the mainstay of a matter. Prophets “among you” and gifts “to you” surround the making of kings. I infer that kingship here activates collective capacity to hold and direct a matter, preparing the command to enter land in 5:21.
2. **Favor demands visible increase.** `ن ع م B001` is bestowed well-being and `B010` means adding and going further. Recollection immediately precedes demanded movement. I infer that remembered favor is meant to generate forward action; a gift not carried onward becomes inert privilege.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Kingship is bestowed capacity awaiting use.** Fixed **م ل ك / B003** (“kingship and dominion”) is explicitly something the people were made, not something self-originating. The next ayah commands entry, 5:22–5:24 expose refusal, and 5:25 contracts Moses’ own *milk* to himself and his brother. I infer that the gift of rule is meant to become agency under command; refusal leaves its title without operative control. “He made you kings” therefore reads as an entrusted capability tested at the threshold, not a guarantee of effortless possession.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 5:25 was the sharpest later correction: “I control only myself and my brother” shows how bestowed kingship contracts when the people refuse to exercise it.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı sesle ortaya çıkarılan söz ve harflerden kurulu sözlü ifade olarak verir. Geçici çerçeve aynı çekirdeği taşıyor; dil organı, hükümdar unvanı ve mecazi yan kullanımlar bu dalın dışında kalır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek işlem, sözü sesli olarak dışa çıkarmaktır.

Ad biçimleri aynı söylenmiş söz alanında toplanır.

root_profile.summary: Bu kök, sesle söze dökme çekirdeğinden konuşma organı, konuşkan kişi, eski unvan, yalan isnat, söylenti, müzakere, hüküm dayatma, iç söz, görüş benimseme, sözsüz belirtme, içten önemseme, teknik tanım ve içe doğan anlam gibi ayrı dallara yayılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi azlığı çokluğun karşıtı olarak verir; ayrıca yoksulluk, düşüklük, bir şeyi az görme ve belirli yapılarda yokluğa ya da seyrekliğe yaklaşan kullanımları açıkça destekler.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol yalnızca sayı ve miktar azlığını ve buna bağlı kullanımları kapsar; yükseklik, kap, taşıma ve titreme anlamlarını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Temel azlık anlamı ile yoksullaşma ve az görme gibi türemiş biçimler birlikte bulunur; yokluk ve seyrekleşme anlamları ise yalnızca belirtilen yapılara bağlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin sayı, miktar ya da ölçü bakımından çok olmayışını bildirir. Bundan yoksulluk ve düşüklük, bir şeyi az sayma veya az gösterme ve belirli yapılarda hiçlik ya da seyrek gerçekleşme anlamları gelişir.

facets.statement: Bir varlığın sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından çok olmayışıdır.
Azlık, kişinin yoksullaşması veya toplum içinde düşük ve değersiz görülmesi sonucuna uzanabilir.
Bir şeyi gerçekte ya da değerlendiren kişinin gözünde az sayma ve az gösterme anlamını taşır.
Belirli olumsuzluk ve sıklık yapılarında hiç yokluğu veya bir eylemin pek seyrek gerçekleşmesini anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar azlığın temel sayı ve miktar karşıtlığında birleşir; yoksulluk ve düşüklük, az sayma ve bazı yapılarda yokluğa yaklaşan kullanım bu çekirdeğin düzenli uzantılarıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sayı, miktar veya ölçünün çok olmayışını bildiren temel anlam için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Çokluğun karşıtı olan sayı ve miktar azlığını doğrudan korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir şeyin sayı veya miktar bakımından çok olmadığının söylendiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Temel azlık durumunu doğal bir Türkçe yapıyla tam olarak verir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir miktarın veya verilen bir şeyin yetersiz ya da küçük sayıldığı değerlendirme bağlamlarında kullanılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyin en üstünü veya başını çekirdek anlam olarak verir; dağın yuvarlak üst bölümü, insan başı ve kılıcın başındaki topuz bu çekirdeğin açık uzmanlaşmalarıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol uzamsal başı ve en üst parçayı bildirir; sayısal azlık ya da büyük kap anlamını içermez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel baş ve en üst bölüm anlamı ile dağ tepesi, insan başı ve kılıç topuzu gibi yapıya bağlı uzmanlaşmalar ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin başını veya en üst bölümünü bildirir. Dağın üstteki yuvarlak parçası, insan başı ve kılıcın sap ucundaki topuz bu uzamsal çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesnenin veya oluşumun başı ya da en üstte bulunan bölümüdür.
Dağın en üstünde yer alan, kimi tanımda yuvarlak biçimli bölümünü adlandırır.
İnsan başı ile kılıcın sap ucundaki başlık veya topuz da aynı üst ve baş kavramıyla adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir şeyin başı ve en üst bölümü üzerinde birleşir; dağ tepesi temel örnektir, insan başı ile kılıç topuzu da aynı biçimsel ve uzamsal çizgide yer alır.

concept_map.definition: Büyük bir küpü veya küpe benzeyen iri kabı bildirir. Belirli bir bölgenin iri küpleri ve iki böyle kabın aldığı miktar bu kap anlamına bağlı özel kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Küpe benzeyen, özellikle sıvı taşımaya veya saklamaya elverişli büyük bir kaptır.
Belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler veya büyük toprak kaplar bu adın tanınmış bir türünü oluşturur.
İki büyük kap, bu iki kabın kendisini veya onların aldığı sıvı miktarını bildiren bir ölçü değeri kazanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar iri bir küp veya büyük kap üzerinde birleşir; tanınmış bölgesel kaplar büyüklüğü örnekler, iki kaplık kullanım ise nesne adını kapasite ölçüsüne taşır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yükü taşıma veya taşıyabilme ile öznenin yükselip harekete geçmesini aynı kolda açıkça toplar; kuşun uçuşa kalkması, göğün yükselmesi ve yolcuların yüklenip ayrılması ayrı katılımcı gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Taşıma, yükselme ve yüklenerek yola koyulma bu kolun sınırıdır; salt sayısal azlık bu anlamlara katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yük taşıma ile yükselme çekirdek çizgileri ayrılır; ağır bulut taşıma, uçuşa kalkma ve yolcuların ayrılması yalnızca kendi özne ve yapılarında geçerlidir.

concept_map.definition: Bir yükü kaldırıp taşıyabilmeyi veya üstlenmeyi ve bir öznenin yükselerek harekete geçmesini bildirir. İkinci çizgi kuşun uçuşa kalkmasını, göğün yükselmesini ve yolcuların yüklenip yola koyulmasını kapsar.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi kaldıracak gücü bulmak, onu taşımak veya yük olarak üstlenmektir.
Bir öznenin aşağıdaki konumundan yükselmesi veya kuş gibi harekete ve uçuşa başlamasıdır.
Yolcuların yüklerini alıp bulundukları yerden ayrılarak yolculuğa başlamasıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir yükü kaldırıp taşıma ile yukarı kalkarak harekete geçme çizgilerini bir araya getirir; kuş, gök, bulut ve yolcu örnekleri katılımcıya göre bu iki çizgiyi somutlaştırır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kişiyi korku veya öfke yüzünden tutan titreme ve silkinişi açıkça tanımlar; genel hareket kararsızlığı değil, duygusal tetikleyicisi bulunan bedensel bir sarsıntı söz konusudur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol insanda korku veya öfkeyle beliren titremeyle sınırlıdır; nesnelerin genel sallanma ve yerinde duramama hali ayrı koldadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Duygudan doğan titreme temel addır; kişiyi titremenin tutması ve öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi yalnızca ilgili yapılara bağlı anlatımlardır.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın korku veya öfke yüzünden titremesi, ürpermesi ya da bedensel olarak silkelenmesidir. Durum, kişiyi bir titreme nöbetinin tutması veya öfkenin titremeyle dışa vurulması biçiminde anlatılabilir.

facets.statement: İnsan bedeninde beliren titreme, ürperti veya istemsiz silkiniş halidir.
Titremenin belirleyici nedeni korku ya da öfkedir.
Belirli yapılarda titremenin kişiyi tutması veya kişinin öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar insandaki titreme ve silkinişte birleşir; korku ile öfke başlıca nedenlerdir ve durum hem kişiyi tutan bir nöbet hem öfkenin bedensel belirtisi olarak anlatılır.

error_profile.preserves: Korku veya öfke koşulunu ve bunun doğurduğu bedensel titremeyi birlikte korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyi hareket ettirip sallandırma, nesnenin bulunduğu yerde kararlı duramaması ve hareketin çıkardığı sesi birlikte verir; bunlar tek bir fiziksel hareket olayının neden, sonuç ve işitsel yönleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol genel fiziksel oynama, kararsızlık ve hareket sesiyle ilgilidir; korku veya öfkeden doğan insana özgü titreme değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım çıplak kolun hareket ettirme, sallanma, yerinde duramama ve hareket sesi anlamlarını kapsar; özel bir yapının anlamı genelleştirilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi hareket ettirerek yerinden oynatmayı ve onun kararsızca sallanıp bulunduğu yerde duramamasını bildirir; bu hareketin çıkardığı ses de aynı olayın işitsel yönüdür.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi hareket ettirip onun yerinden oynamasına ve sarsılmasına neden olmaktır.
Nesnenin bulunduğu yerde sabit kalmayıp sallanması, oynaması veya düzensiz hareket etmesidir.
Sallanma ve yer değiştirme sırasında çıkan ses, hareket olayının işitsel belirtisi olarak adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar dışarıdan hareket ettirme ile nesnenin kararsızca sallanıp yerinde duramaması üzerinde birleşir; hareketin sesi bu fiziksel olayın ayrılmaz işitsel belirtisi olarak eklenir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, sözcüğün temel olarak kadınlar dışındaki erkekler topluluğunu anlattığını, kadınların ancak ikincil biçimde kapsama girebildiğini ve insan dışı varlıklara aktarılabildiğini gösterir. Bu nedenle genel ve cinsiyetçe sınırsız bir topluluk adı olarak sunulmamalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Temel kapsam erkekler topluluğudur; kadınların katılımı ve insan dışına aktarım ikincil kullanımlardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, temel topluluk anlamını bağlı anlatımlardaki yandaş ve soy çevresi anlamından ayırır.

concept_map.definition: Temelde erkeklerden oluşan insan topluluğudur; bir erkeğin yandaş ve yakın soy çevresini de anlatabilir. Kadınların topluluğa bağlı olarak kapsanması ve sözün insan dışı varlıklara aktarılması ikincildir.

facets.statement: Temel gönderge, kadınlardan ayrı düşünülen erkekler topluluğudur.
Bir erkeğin yandaşları ile yakın soy çevresi, kadınların bağlı olarak kapsanması ve insan dışına aktarım bu çekirdeğe bağlıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çekirdeği erkekler topluluğudur; bir erkeğin yandaşları ve yakın soy çevresi bu kapsamda yer alır. Kadınların bağlı biçimde kapsanması ile insan dışı varlıklara aktarım ayrıca kaydedilir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Erkeklerden oluşan topluluğu ve buna bağlı yandaş ya da soy çevresini birlikte karşılayan en kısa açıklamadır.

error_profile.preserves: Erkek topluluğu çekirdeğini ve bağlı yakın çevre kapsamını korur.

error_profile.preserves: Temel cinsiyet sınırını ve topluluk anlamını korur.
